{
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "Primary endpoint analysis not specified",
      "quote": "The primary endpoint of Study 20190009 is progression-free Survival (PFS).",
      "page": 38,
      "section": "2.1.2 Primary Endpoints",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "critical",
      "explanation": "The primary endpoint is defined but no statistical analysis method (e.g., Cox model, Kaplan-Meier) is stated in this section. The protocol must specify the primary analysis for PFS.",
      "fix": "Add a description of the primary analysis method for PFS, including the statistical model and handling of censoring."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing estimand attributes for secondary endpoints",
      "quote": "The key secondary endpoints are OS, objective response rate (ORR), patient-reported outcomes (PRO), including change from baseline (cycle 1 day 1) over time to week 12 in disease related symptoms (dyspnea, cough, and chest pain), physical functioning, and health related quality of life (QOL).",
      "page": 38,
      "section": "2.1.3 Key Secondary Endpoints",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The key secondary endpoints are listed but the estimand attributes (population, variable, intercurrent events, summary measure) are not fully described for each endpoint in this section. Only OS and ORR have estimand details later, but PRO endpoints lack explicit intercurrent event strategies and summary measures.",
      "fix": "Provide a complete estimand for each key secondary endpoint, including intercurrent event handling and summary measures."
    },
    {
      "title": "Incomplete intercurrent event strategy for PFS",
      "quote": "PFS is censored at the date of last evaluable assessment before or on start of new anti-cancer therapy.",
      "page": 48,
      "section": "3 Objectives and Endpoints",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The intercurrent event strategy for PFS is described as censoring at start of new therapy, but the estimand framework section (Section 9.4.2.2) is referenced but not provided here. The strategy may be inconsistent with the primary estimand description which says 'before or on start of new anti-cancer therapy' but does not specify the treatment policy strategy for other intercurrent events like death.",
      "fix": "Clarify the intercurrent event handling for PFS, including death and other events, and ensure consistency with the estimand framework."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing analysis for DOR, TTR, DCR",
      "quote": "To compare efficacy of AMG 510 versus docetaxel as assessed by: duration of response (DOR), time to response (TTR), and disease control rate (DCR)",
      "page": 48,
      "section": "3 Objectives and Endpoints",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The objectives list DOR, TTR, and DCR as secondary endpoints, but no analysis methods are stated for these endpoints in the provided text. The protocol must specify how these will be analyzed.",
      "fix": "Add statistical analysis methods for DOR, TTR, and DCR, including estimands and summary measures."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing analysis for safety endpoint",
      "quote": "To compare the safety and tolerability of AMG 510 versus docetaxel",
      "page": 48,
      "section": "3 Objectives and Endpoints",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The safety objective is stated but no safety endpoints or analysis methods are described in the provided text. The protocol must define safety endpoints and their statistical analysis.",
      "fix": "Add a section describing safety endpoints (e.g., adverse events, laboratory abnormalities) and their analysis methods."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing analysis for PK endpoint",
      "quote": "To characterize the pharmacokinetics (PK) of AMG 510 and its major metabolites",
      "page": 48,
      "section": "3 Objectives and Endpoints",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The PK objective is stated but no PK endpoints or analysis methods are provided. The protocol must specify PK parameters and their statistical analysis.",
      "fix": "Add a section describing PK endpoints (e.g., AUC, Cmax) and their analysis methods."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing sample size inputs",
      "quote": "The primary endpoint of Study 20190009 is progression-free Survival (PFS).",
      "page": 38,
      "section": "2.1.2 Primary Endpoints",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "critical",
      "explanation": "The protocol does not provide sample size calculation inputs (e.g., assumed hazard ratio, event rate, alpha, power) in the provided text. The sample size section is missing.",
      "fix": "Add a sample size section with all inputs and assumptions for the primary endpoint."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing multiplicity adjustment",
      "quote": "The key secondary endpoints are OS, objective response rate (ORR), patient-reported outcomes (PRO), including change from baseline (cycle 1 day 1) over time to week 12 in disease related symptoms (dyspnea, cough, and chest pain), physical functioning, and health related quality of life (QOL).",
      "page": 38,
      "section": "2.1.3 Key Secondary Endpoints",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "Multiple key secondary endpoints are listed, but no multiplicity control strategy (e.g., hierarchical testing, alpha allocation) is described. This is a critical gap for confirmatory testing.",
      "fix": "Add a section describing the multiplicity adjustment strategy for key secondary endpoints."
    }
  ]
}
